title.en: Wishes and Regrets (I wish / If only)
title.es: Deseos y arrepentimientos (I wish / If only)

text.en: I wish and If only express a wish or regret that does not come true. The tense steps one back: past simple for the present (“I wish I had more time.”), past perfect for the past (“I wish I had studied more.”), would for something you want to change (“I wish it would stop raining.”). The Spanish “ojalá tuviera”, “ojalá hubiera sabido” and “ojalá dejara de llover” match these closely.
text.es: I wish y If only expresan un deseo o un arrepentimiento que no se cumple. El tiempo verbal retrocede un paso: pasado simple para el presente («I wish I had more time.»), past perfect para el pasado («I wish I had studied more.»), would para algo que se quiere cambiar («I wish it would stop raining.»). El «ojalá tuviera», el «ojalá hubiera sabido» y el «ojalá dejara de llover» del español les corresponden de cerca.

title.en: Regret about the present: wish + past simple
title.es: Arrepentimiento sobre el presente: wish + pasado simple

text.en: The present situation is not what you want. With be, were is the formal form and was is the everyday form: “I wish I were taller.”
text.es: La situación actual no es la que quieres. Con be, were es la forma formal y was la cotidiana: «I wish I were taller.»

tr.en: I wish I didn't have to work today.
tr.es: Ojalá no tuviera que trabajar hoy.

text.en: To wish for an ability you do not have, use could: “I wish I could fly.” For a real future possibility use hope, not wish: “I hope you can come.”
text.es: Para desear una habilidad que no tienes se usa could: «I wish I could fly.» Para una posibilidad real en el futuro se usa hope, no wish: «I hope you can come.»

tr.en: I hope you can come tomorrow.

title.en: Regret about the past: wish + past perfect
title.es: Arrepentimiento sobre el pasado: wish + past perfect

text.en: Something happened (or did not happen) and you want it to have been different: wish + had + participle.
text.es: Algo ocurrió (o no ocurrió) y quieres que hubiera sido distinto: wish + had + participio.

tr.en: I wish I had studied more.

examples.es: She wishes she hadn't said that.

tr.en: She wishes she hadn't said that.

title.en: A complaint, something you want changed: wish + would
title.es: Una queja, algo que quieres cambiar: wish + would

text.en: For other people’s behavior or things you cannot control, use would. Not for yourself: not “I wish I would”, but “I wish I could”.
text.es: Para la conducta de otras personas o cosas que no controlas se usa would. No para uno mismo: no «I wish I would», sino «I wish I could».

examples.es: I wish you would stop talking.

tr.en: I wish you would stop talking.

title.es: If only: un deseo más fuerte

text.en: If only takes the same tenses as wish, but it is more emotional: “If only I had listened!”
text.es: If only pide los mismos tiempos que wish, pero es más emotivo: «If only I had listened!»

examples.es: If only I had more money!

tr.en: If only I had more money!
If only I had listened!

text.en: After wish there is no will and no present tense: not “I wish I have more time”, but “I wish I had more time”. The step back stays even when the regret is about the present.
text.es: Después de wish no va will ni presente: no «I wish I have more time», sino «I wish I had more time». El retroceso se mantiene aunque el arrepentimiento sea sobre el presente.

text.en: The Spanish “ojalá puedas venir” (a real chance) is hope, and “ojalá pudieras venir” (little chance) is wish: “I hope you can come” and “I wish you could come”.
text.es: El «ojalá puedas venir» (hay posibilidad real) es hope, y el «ojalá pudieras venir» (poca posibilidad) es wish: «I hope you can come» y «I wish you could come».

speak.en: «I wish» and «If only» express a wish or regret that does not come true. The tense steps one back. For the present, the past simple is used: «I wish I had more time». For the past, the past perfect is used: «I wish I had studied more». For something you want to change, «would» is used: «I wish it would stop raining». For an ability you do not have, «could» is used: «I wish I could fly». For a real chance in the future you need «hope», not «wish»: «I hope you can come».
speak.es: «I wish» y «If only» expresan un deseo o un arrepentimiento que no se cumple. El tiempo verbal retrocede un paso. Para el presente se usa el pasado simple: «I wish I had more time». Para el pasado se usa el past perfect: «I wish I had studied more». Para algo que se quiere cambiar se usa «would»: «I wish it would stop raining». Para una habilidad que no se tiene se usa «could»: «I wish I could fly». Para una posibilidad real en el futuro hace falta «hope», no «wish»: «I hope you can come».
